subject: Novaterra discovery 7 consensus map + next-step asks
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@novaterra.io>, Mark Lively <mlively@novaterra.io>, Kara Liu <kara.liu@novaterra.io>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@novaterra.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Novaterra discovery 7 consensus map + next-step asks

Elena / Mark / Kara / Priya 00 thank you for the time this morning. Good conversation 00 summarized below so we have a shared picture and clear next steps. I've attached the raw call notes (novaterra-discovery-notes.pdf) and a starter ROI-template.xlsx we can iterate on.

Quick summary (consensus):
- Champion: Elena Soto (Head of ML) 00 primary driver is lowering inference cost and improving p95 latency on their search product.
- Economic buyer: Mark Lively (CFO) 00 wants committed pricing with predictable monthly spend and a clear P&L impact.
- Security: Kara Liu (Dir, InfoSec) 00 SOC2 + encryption + audit logs non-negotiable; will want a brief security checklist.
- Procurement: Priya Desai 00 standard SOW review window ~60 days; prefers purchase order route.

Explicit decision criteria called out on the call:
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token avg workloads (US-East pilot).
- Data residency: pilot must run in US-East; longer-term options for multi-region.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II + customer-facing audit logs and KMS integrations.
- Commercial: target committed capacity band discussed $200k$400k ARR for pilot/year 1, with option to convert to Dedicated.

Promised deliverables / asks (owners / dates):
1) Technical brief mapping Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Novaterra needs (Ben + Rishi) 00 deliver by Wed EOD 3/4.
2) Demo agenda + proposed pilot scope (30-day pilot goals, success metrics) 00 I'll draft and share by Tue 3/2 (demo-agenda.md attached).
3) ROI workbook populated with their estimate inputs (Rishi to own update; Elena & Mark to add numbers) 00 target 3/6.
4) Security checklist & evidence pack (SOC2, encryption, logs) 00 Kara requested sample evidence; Ben to collate initial checklist by 3/5.
5) Procurement path confirmation (Priya) 00 outline payment terms and preferred contracting timeline; Priya, please confirm.

Immediate asks from our side to Novaterra team:
- Elena / Mark: can you share a small anonymized sample payload + avg token lengths so we can run a realistic latency estimation?
- Kara: who is the vendor security contact and preferred template for evidence intake (e.g., shared drive or secure portal)?
- Priya: confirm preferred PO terms and any required vendor onboarding docs.

I've put links to the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder in the metadata. Attaching the discovery notes and ROI template for quick reference. I'll follow up with a proposed demo time once we align on scope.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Thanks Sofia 00 this captures the call. We're aligned on the criteria. A couple notes from our side:
- We can share a sanitized 1MB payload (search query + doc snippets) by EOD today; will include typical token lengths.
- Procurement: Priya confirms a 60-day review and will need a draft SOW + security checklist to begin vendor onboarding.
- Security: Kara will coordinate evidence intake; prefer secure upload to our portal. Kara 00 I'll loop you into the portal invite separately.

I've attached Novaterra-internal-priorities.docx which shows where this project sits in our FY26 roadmap (priority 2). Mark is copied for the commercial/ROI inputs.

We'd like a short (30-40 minute) technical demo next week. Can you propose two time slots?

Cheers,
Elena

elena@novaterra.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Novaterra discovery 7 consensus map + next-step asks 

Elena / team 00 thanks. I've attached a short technical brief (novaterra-technical-brief.pdf) that maps our runtime options to the decision criteria:
- Hosted (fastest time to pilot): supports US-East tenancy, can meet p95 ~120-160ms depending on model and batching. Good for quick proof-of-value.
- Dedicated (best for predictable unit cost): reserved GPU pools, deterministic latency at scale; p95 can be kept <=150ms with configured autoscale and KV-cache priming. Good for conversion after pilot.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): supports strict residency + KMS integration; more lead time.

Immediate asks for a realistic latency estimate: please upload the sanitized payload to the Drive folder and include one representative model checkpoint size (or a rough token-per-request distribution). If you can't share the checkpoint, tell us the base model family and average sequence length.

For security evidence: Kara, I can produce the SOC2 summary and a sample audit-log extract. What's the preferred format for the audit log (CSV with timestamps or JSON)?

Demo options (proposed):
- Wed 3/3 10:00-10:40 PT
- Thu 3/4 14:00-14:40 PT

I'll also push a preliminary pricing-estimate.csv into the Drive (CC Aisha for commercial headcount and discount rationale).

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

- Populate baseline (current infra cost + estimated Redwood savings) by Fri 3/6.
- Prepare a two-slide summary that Elena can use to brief Mark and the finance committee.

Sofia 00 if Wed 3/3 at 10am works for Novaterra I'll lock that demo and prep a short demo script focused on latency tradeoffs and cost delta. Ben 00 can you bring a short KV-cache demo and a cost-per-token comparison for their payload after you run the backlog sample?

Thanks,
Rishi
